reviews.comment: All in all, really great professor, his lectures can sometimes go on a ramble, and he is not the best lecturer, but his exams are similar, if not identical, to problem sets. He curves a lot and is just a really sweet person.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gronberg is one of the brightest professors at A&M, not once during the course was he asked a question he did not immediately have answers for. The class wasn't too hard, exams are 75% of the grade, in class quizzes are 25%. He curves generously. Problem sets very similar to the exam are posted along with slides. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice & answers questions asked in lecture. Won't put material he hasn't covered in class in exams or quizzes. Quizzes in class & not always announced. Lectures do tend to go over time. Gives practice problems that are similar to exam problems with answer keys. I did fine on exams by looking at practice problems and going back through the textbook.

Gronberg is really sweet, but his lectures go long and were difficult to learn from. TA was no help, and the free responses on the test were often confusing and hard to get full credit on. I know Meer is also difficult, I recommend taking Econ for credit outside A&M.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a good professor, and definitely a sweet person. The lectures can be a little tiresome/long, and usually I had to do most of my learning on my own. Beware that he might go 15 minutes over the allotted class time lecturing. You will also likely be behind on the syllabus, but he only tests over the chapters he covers in class.
He's cool! Honestly most of the learning I did was through the textbook, but the class is definetely an easy A.

Professor Gronberg is a very smart, kind professor. Cares about his students a lot. Lectures could get a little long-winded and he does not have the most interactive slides. Understanding the homework and practice problems are crucial to doing well on exams. The TAs are not the best and the grading breakdown of the class make it tough to get an A.

I love professor Gronberg as a person, but man, is his class dreadful. I attended every lecture, and his exams were all free responses (required a lot of writing to get full credit). He rambles a lot. I studied hard, took great notes, and his problem sets and exams were still very difficult. A great person, not so great professor.

He's nice but says so much without saying anything at all in lectures+TA graded hard so everyone in our hnrs section was suffering. Though we were all trying hard, averages were B's for prob sets and the 1st exam, and office hrs were mostly him rambling as well. Always behind on the syllabus+PS' sometimes had stuff not covered yet

Class set up with 3 tests (25% each) and 6 problem sets (in total 25% of grade, but he drops one). He picks one of the 5 questions from the PSs to grade so if you did poorly on one and he chose that, you're out of luck. BUT the PSs are just like the test so if you study those and the sample test, you'll do fine on the tests

Professor Gronberg is great! Out of my years at TAMU he is by far the best Econ professor I have had. He really wants the best for his students and is willing to communicate with them. He is extremely detailed and knowledgeable. I do not regret taking him, and would recommend taking his class to other Econ majors!
Class itself is pretty chill, he talks A LOT though. The tests normally have some "twist" to what we've actually learned in class and hes perfectly happy with a low class average so that kinda sucks

He is a really nice guy. Goes out of his way to learn the names and faces of everyone in the class. He will ramble on about topics, but he does a good job of keeping people engaged and teaching the material. Gives homework most weeks, but doing the homework and the practice review is very helpful for the test. Good choice for 412
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, but he does drag on forever about each topic. We only covered about 1/3 of what was on the syllabus because of how much he rambles. The class was at 8:45 AM, so sometimes it was definitely hard to stay awake. We also had a quiz almost every class. He is one of my favorite professors though. He is super sweet and helpful!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS
